proposal:
STATUS: nothing executed; all numbers are hand derivations from the supplied code. No polynomial-SAT claim.

A. AUDIT
A1 (compression.py). Blocks are rebuilt from every dense original clause. Each block checks C_S(x)=Q_S(Px) on all 2^|S| local points with forms confined to the block mask. P*L=I is checked entrywise, so P is onto and F=Q o P gives equisatisfiability. Every skip returns the untouched input. Check cost is at most 256*(block literals) per block plus r^2*n. I found no soundness defect; the alleged omitted-block bug is absent.
A2 (cache key). step() is memoised on the raw restrict() tuple, not on canon_plus output. My hand model of last round's receipt (PT_5, paired order) has 18 step evaluations. Exactly two hit the cache, only because their raw clause order happened to be canonical already. That yields 16 IALH calls, 1120 windows, 28360 tuples, 4 refutations and 12 DP steps, all equal to the receipt (post-hoc agreement). Repeated IALH work is therefore an ordering accident. Memoising refute and elim_plus on the canonical formula is an exact, pure-function fix.
A3. Quotient branch order is the greedy tie-break index (coverage, popcount, mask). It carries no structure; Neon58's 8-versus-2 is this artifact.

B. ORDER-BY-TWIN (OBT): certificate-free
Every full order is exact, so choosing the order has no soundness burden. For canonical F, call {x,y} a twin edge when two distinct assignments of (x,y) give the same non-UNSAT canon(F|x,y). Branch contiguously through connected components of the twin graph (size cap 4), components listed by least index. Change points: variables(quotient) and the fallback order. Cost: 4 canon calls per co-occurring pair. Neon58 quotient: 120 pairs, 480 canon calls on 48 clauses, about 10^6 subset tests. At 32 variables and 512 clauses it is about 5*10^8, so it needs gating or indexed subsumption.
On the pair-transversal family PT_k the twin edges are exactly the 2k pairs. (0,1),(1,0),(1,1) leave identical residuals because the shrunk transversal clauses subsume their siblings. (0,0) leaves the clauses (b_j or b_j') plus the other side.

C. RESTRICTED WORK CLAIM (L-PT, hand-derived)
Let m=2^(k+1) negative clauses, k>=3.
- Pair-contiguous order: at most 2 states per layer and 5k+1 step evaluations. The (0,0) child dies by an empty IALH table (k<=5) or by size-nonincreasing DP (first members, then second members, at most m/2 non-tautological resolvents per elimination). Total O~(m^2) clause-pair operations plus one capped IALH per step.
- First-members-first order: states double until two pairs remain, then DP closes every child. Peak 2^(k-2)=m/8, total O~(m^3).
So OBT removes one factor m (cubic to quadratic). It is not an exponential rescue: PT_k is polynomial in encoded size under either order.
Fixture: last round's PT_5 clauses, order changed to first members first. Predicted: compression skipped (all_variables_in_odd_blocks), core no_clauses_removed, layers 2,4,8,0, peak 8, UNSAT. Secondary, lower confidence: 31 IALH calls, 1 refutation, 197 DP steps, about 7.9*10^4 tuples, about 10 s. The paired order on these clauses measured peak 2.

D. CEILING AND ONE STEP OUTSIDE IT
OBT should find no twin edge on pigeonhole, and if MT2 holds no order helps there. UP, subsumption, SCC substitution, DP, below-pruning, residual merging and mod-d lattice leaves are all bounded-depth-Frege-plus-counting inferences. Pigeonhole needs an inequality count.
CLIQUE-FARKAS leaf (CF, unimplemented). Rows: sum of literals >= 1 for every clause; sum over K <= 1 for every greedily found clique K in the graph whose edges are binary clauses (not l or not l'); 0<=x<=1. Certificate: nonnegative rationals y with yA=0 and yb>0, Fraction-checked like verify_dual, plus |K|^2 clause look-ups per clique. Sound because every row holds in every model. PHP_h: unit multipliers on h+1 pigeon clauses and h hole cliques give 0>=1; check cost O(h^3), linear in the input. Added clauses only add rows, so a found certificate stays valid under arbitrary extras; discovery does not (see attack 6).
Independent-test predictions: CF refutes PHP h=4,5,6 at the root with 2h+1 unit multipliers and zero IALH windows. OBT plus canonical memo gives Neon58 peak 2 with no repeated canonical IALH input.

E. NOT HANDLED
CF is inert on Neon58 (x=1/2 satisfies every wide row). OBT is inert on pigeonhole, on Neon57 and on twin-free kernel-free families. Large twin components need the unchecked OR-gate contraction of Fable73. No bound is given for exact LP discovery.
missing_theorem:
MT1 (restricted, provable by hand, Lean-ready): L-PT for both orders. It needs (i) IALH returns UNKNOWN on every mixed PT state: each window table contains a point with all unit neighbours, up to one twin swap, so its lattice is Z^k and no row is emitted; (ii) no DP step fires before two pairs remain; (iii) the DP closing chain never sticks.

MT2 (ceiling; conditional parameterized bound): every UNSAT v5 run with N step evaluations, under any order including OBT, yields a constant-depth Frege refutation with Count_p axioms of size poly(B)*N. Lines are negated residual CNFs. A lattice dual with denominator d becomes a linear refutation modulo a prime power dividing d over 5-local constraints. If proved, the known pigeonhole lower bounds for bounded-depth Frege with counting axioms (Pitassi-Beame-Impagliazzo, Krajicek-Pudlak-Woods, Beame-Pitassi, Beame-Riis; cited from memory, unverified here) give N >= exp(h^eps)/poly(B) on PHP_h. This is a statement about the v5 rule set, not about SAT.

MT3 (the open gap): (a) a polynomial bit bound for the exact LP that finds y; (b) a structural characterisation of the UNSAT CNFs with polynomial total work under twin order + lattice + CF. A bound for all CNF would make this composite certificate system polynomially bounded and automatable, hence NP=coNP at least. So each leaf is a restricted result, and the obstruction is exactly the next family outside it. CF is cutting-planes rank 0, so clique-colouring-type and random k-CNF families remain.
self_attack:
1. OBT is dynamic twin detection, a form of functional decomposition; known. On PT_k it gains only a factor m. I have not constructed a bounded-width family with an exponential order gap.
2. The twin test can cost 5*10^8 subset checks at the caps, more than the search it saves.
3. My reproduction of the receipt is post hoc. The fixture's secondary counts rest on hand window enumeration and may be off. Peak 8 depends on IALH returning UNKNOWN on 14 mixed states no receipt has seen; one unexpected lattice row lowers it. About 10 s is within a factor 2 of the 20 s cap; a timeout is inconclusive.
4. I assume the trusted Neon58 order [1,9,3,11,...] is pair-contiguous in quotient numbering; I cannot verify the numbering.
5. MT2: residual caching with weakening can exceed resolution (Beame-Impagliazzo-Pitassi-Segerlind), so the ceiling is bounded-depth Frege, not resolution. The SCC and DP simulations are sketched only, and the counting-axiom lower bound for composite d needs a source check.
6. CF is old (LP with clique cuts). Greedy clique cover can split hole cliques when extra binary clauses are present; then the LP is feasible and CF returns UNKNOWN. Edge rows alone do not refute PHP (x=1/2). Maximum clique is NP-hard, so discovery is restricted.
7. These are two mechanisms, not one invariant: CF does nothing for Neon58 and OBT nothing for PHP.
mechanism_signature: Three exact, separately checkable pieces. (1) Certificate-free ORDER-BY-TWIN: branch contiguously through components of the residual-collision graph. (2) Canonical-key memo of IALH and elim. (3) CLIQUE-FARKAS leaf: nonnegative rational multipliers over clause rows and binary-clause clique rows, Fraction-checked. Work accounting: step evaluations times (capped IALH + O~(m^2) DP attempts). Conjectured ceiling for everything except (3): bounded-depth Frege with counting axioms.
delta_from_prior: Round 101 changed state merging (dual keys, rho width, conjecture NC). This round changes no merge rule and rewrites no clause. New: (i) cache-key audit with an exact hand reproduction of the receipt counts; (ii) a soundness-free order selector with a defined twin graph and stated cost; (iii) both-order analysis of PT_k showing the gap is one polynomial factor, with a pinned-v5 fixture (peak 8 against measured 2); (iv) a proof-system ceiling (MT2) and a Farkas leaf outside it for pigeonhole. No factoring or contraction is re-proposed.
